blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Mauryan Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya) after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty.
The administration was highly centralized and divided into provinces governed by royal princes (Kumaras).
Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism after witnessing the devastation of the Kalinga War in 261 BCE and formulated the policy of Dhamma.
Ashokan Edicts, written mainly in Prakrit using the Brahmi script, are the earliest written historical records in the Indian subcontinent.
The Mauryan economy was supported by agriculture, state-regulated trade, and a standardized coinage system based on silver coins (Pana).

blocks.content: The Mauryan Empire was the first empire in Indian history that achieved political unification of a large part of the Indian subcontinent. Founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BC, the Mauryan Empire laid the foundation of centralized administration, a vast standing army, state-controlled economy, and an efficient bureaucratic system. The empire reached its zenith under Ashoka the Great.
Mauryan history is reconstructed using a wide range of literary, epigraphic, and foreign sources.
Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya (Kautilya), overthrew the Nanda dynasty and established the Mauryan Empire. His reign marked the beginning of imperial rule in India.
He defeated Seleucus Nicator in 305 BC and secured north-western territories. A matrimonial alliance was concluded, and Megasthenes was sent as ambassador to his court.
In his later life, Chandragupta accepted Jainism under Bhadrabahu and performed Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
Bindusara expanded the empire southwards up to the Deccan. Greek writers referred to him as Amitrochates (slayer of enemies).
All men are my children. What I desire for my own children, that they be provided with all welfare and happiness in this world and the next, I desire for all men.
Ashoka was the greatest Mauryan ruler. His reign represents a unique blend of imperial power and moral governance.
The devastating Kalinga War transformed Ashoka’s outlook. He renounced aggressive warfare and adopted a policy of Dhamma.
Ashoka’s Dhamma was a moral code emphasizing non-violence, tolerance, respect for elders, kindness to servants, and harmony among religious sects.
Ashoka appointed special officers called Dhamma Mahamatras to propagate moral values and look after the welfare of people.

blocks.content: The Mauryan administration was highly centralized and bureaucratic.
The king was assisted by Mantriparishad. Important officials included Amatyas, Mahamatras, and Adhyakshas.
Provinces were governed by Kumara or Aryaputra. Important provinces included Taxila and Ujjain.
Megasthenes mentions six committees managing urban administration.
The state exercised control over agriculture, trade, mining, and forests.
Land revenue (Bhaga) was generally one-sixth of the produce.
Punch-marked coins were widely used. Internal and foreign trade flourished.

items: The 13th Major Rock Edict explicitly describes Ashoka's victory over Kalinga and his subsequent remorse and devotion to Dhamma.
Megasthenes was the Seleucid ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya's court and wrote 'Indica', which mentions a seven-caste system in Mauryan society.
The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath was adopted as the National Emblem of India in 1950.
Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' is a treatise on statecraft and political economy detailing the Saptanga theory of the state.

blocks.content: The Mauryan army consisted of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants. A strong espionage system was maintained as described in Arthashastra.
Mauryan art is characterized by polish and monumental scale.
Important examples include Ashokan pillars with lion capitals, stupas like Sanchi, and rock-cut caves such as Barabar caves.
After Ashoka, weak rulers, financial strain, and administrative over-centralization led to the decline. The last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha was assassinated by Pushyamitra Shunga.
